# Ayush Dutta - Security Researcher & Developer

> Security researcher & developer. Platform & security at Atlan, Linux Foundation LFX'26 mentee at Magma. NixOS, agentic harnesses, reproducible machines, accessible security. Zero-JS portfolio drawn with ascii.rest at berzi.one.

## Personal Introduction

Yes, I'm Ayush Dutta and you will love this story.

Once, a kid decided he wanted to understand how things break. Not to break them for bad, but to learn how to fix them even better.

Now I spend my days at Atlan, on platform and security, in an environment that introduced me to problems and tools I could not have reached on my own. And I contribute to Magma through the Linux Foundation, an open source mentee working on the future of telecom.

My philosophy is simple: Don't tell me your title, show me your work.

## Chapter 1: The Breaking

It started with curiosity. I wanted to know what makes systems fail.

My first industry internship came from breaking into a startup's admin panel. The founder was kind enough to let me intern, find, report and fix more bugs in their products. Then I worked for a consultancy building hackable environments sold to clients like OffSec and HackTheBox, analysing CVEs and 0days, packaging them into VMs and testing them on Proxmox.

## Chapter 2: The Building

While all this breaking was happening, I started building too.

**lemonx**: An agentic AI testing platform that autonomously generates, executes and fixes unit, integration and E2E tests for TypeScript/JavaScript codebases. Runs on GitHub Actions.

**yuki-code**: A Nix-based harness for reproducible agent sessions, so an AI engineering team's environment is a function you can evaluate again tomorrow.

**berzinix**: A fully-declarative NixOS setup on flakes and home-manager, running Hyprland on an NVIDIA GPU. Nothing on my machine is accidental.

**agentic-aeo-skills**: An LLM-first AEO analysis skillset with 6 specialized sub-skills, 6 specialist agents and evidence-collecting utility scripts, compatible with Codex, Claude, Gemini and OpenCode.

**hackfish**: Swarm intelligence to predict your next hackathon winning project.

**shovel**: A memory-efficient, fast web crawler written with goroutines.

Most of these are experiments built from niche technology, or built to prove a point that it can be done.

## Chapter 3: The Leading

I believe the best security education is accessible. I do all kinds of community work to help people get started with cybersecurity as easily as possible.

I founded Google Developer Groups at my campus. Grew from zero to 1100 members in 9 months.

I lead Next Tech Lab. A QS Reimagine Education awarded student society running since 2017.

I advise for FOSS United, AWS Cloud Club, and Hackshastra.

## Chapter 4: The Proving

I don't collect degrees. I collect proof.

Currently pursuing B.Tech at SRM University-AP. The classroom taught me the least. What mattered most was showing up to different communities.

- Linux Foundation Mentorship (LFX'26) at Magma
- GitHub Pull Shark x2, YOLO, Quickdraw, Public Sponsor
- 220+ GitHub followers
